title: Where does an expedition's team run: as hub agents under a Lead, or inside one agent?
lead: Should each expedition role run as its own hub agent, started by a Lead with a few scoped tools, rather than as hidden helpers inside one agent? I recommend hub agents, as your spec does: you see the whole team on the map and the report's figures are measured, not guessed.
for_you: Each running expedition shows as one cluster on the live map and one folded row in the thread list; you can open any member
Time, tokens and cost per role in the report come from the log, so the budget stop and the figures are real
The orchestrator stays out of it until the one summary at the end

for_you.text: Nothing to set up; the seven role files ship with the hub's starter types

context: Matt's Expedition module spec (2026-11-15, memo M044) leaves this open (section 12) and recommends a hub worker with scoped tools (section 4.1). The reference run used Claude Code subagents. Scoping (2026-11-16) found the subagent route can't meet two of the spec's own guarantees: usage per role (the SDK reports usage per model, not per subagent) and per-agent permission and freeze rules. The advisor checkpoint agreed with A.

options.name: Hub agents under a Lead
options.summary: The orchestrator starts the Lead; the Lead starts the other roles as normal hub agents with four tools limited to its own expedition (start, message, retire, list). Every role has a thread, logs its own usage and goes through the permission check.
pros: Whole team visible on the map; measured cost per role; per-agent rules for the frozen test and no-merge
cons: The largest build (phase 2 of 6); 7 to 10 agents per run need folding in the thread list

options.name: Helpers inside one agent
options.summary: One hub agent, the Lead, runs every role as a Claude Code subagent, as in the reference run.
cons: Roles invisible on the map; cost per role can't be measured; every permission request lands on the Lead

options.name: Mixed
options.summary: Hub agents for Builder, Verifier, Skeptic and Advisor; gatherers as helpers inside the Lead.
cons: The gatherers are the ones browsing the web, so their requests and spend are the part you most want separated

recommendation: A, as the spec recommends: it is the only option that keeps the budget stop and the per-role figures honest.
change_mind: If the phase 2 build turns out far larger than planned, a short B spike could come first, but not as the version you rely on.

settles.value: a long-running team job runs each role as a visible hub agent under a lead with tools scoped to its own team

images.caption: An expedition on the live map: the Lead with its team around it, two thin arcs for time and budget
